comparator.name: Economics and Governance (Bachelor Economie en Beleid)
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official handbook defines 180 EC: a 111-EC compulsory common part, a 3-EC restricted mathematics/statistics choice, one 24-EC thesis track and 42 EC of open electives. The Economics thesis track is selected by the official-order tie-break and is completed with the first two listed 6-EC restricted options plus the 12-EC thesis.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target is the generic Economics and Governance bachelor. Its two 24-EC thesis tracks, Economics and Governance, are equally formal and neither is named by the target. The Economics track appears first in the current official structure and is selected neutrally, independently of UCR fit.

alternatives.label: Economics, public policy & institutions
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines microeconomics, macroeconomics, public economics, econometrics and behavioural economics with politics, law, sociology, inequality and institutions.
alternatives.concept: A balanced closest feasible response combining economics, quantitative analysis, public institutions, politics, law and social inequality to examine how economic choices become public policy.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad closest match, this route replaces accounting, marketing, business strategy, international business, product design, machine learning, probability and finance with comparative politics, sociology, qualitative methods, political philosophy, human rights, constitutional law, sustainability governance, EU politics, social theory, persuasive communication, peace and conflict, and historical research. The resulting curriculum is organised around institutions and policy rather than firms and business functions.
progression: Economics, politics, sociology, law, data and ethics foundations precede microeconomics, public economics, econometrics, EU politics, inequality and advanced policy analysis. All formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass, with nine 300-level courses.

alternatives.label: Economics, trade & quantitative analysis
alternatives.labelReason: The completed programme is dominated by microeconomics, macroeconomics, econometrics, behavioural economics, finance, data science, mathematics and computation.
alternatives.concept: Develops the evidenced Economics direction through microeconomics, macroeconomics and trade, econometrics, behavioural economics, finance, mathematics, data science and computational analysis.
alternatives.distinctness: This route makes formal economics, trade, data and quantitative analysis the organising priority. It differs from the balanced programme by well over four courses and 30 EC.
progression: Economics, business, data and mathematical foundations precede intermediate microeconomics, public economics, econometrics, behavioural economics and quantitative analysis. All formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass, with six 300-level courses.

alternatives.label: Public governance, institutions & policy
alternatives.concept: Develops the evidenced Policy direction through comparative politics, public economics, law, governance institutions, policy processes, sociology, organisational analysis and mixed research methods.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed programme centres comparative politics, public economics, law, institutions, policy, sociology, organisations and public communication.
progression: Politics, law, economics, sociology, communication and methods foundations precede public economics, EU politics, comparative law, environmental governance and advanced policy study. All formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass, with seven 300-level courses.
alternatives.distinctness: This route makes governance institutions, law and policy processes the organising priority. It differs from both economics-led programmes by at least seven courses and 52.5 EC.

selection.assessment: The closest programme integrates economics with public institutions and policy. The official Economics and Policy emphases support two further coherent, feasible and pairwise-distinct alternatives. Production stops at the three-alternative maximum.

notes.text: WUR offers a dedicated economics-and-governance curriculum with sequenced economics, econometrics, public administration, specialist policy courses and a thesis. UCR can combine substantial economics, quantitative analysis, politics, law and sustainability governance, but it does not reproduce the same specialist sequence course for course.
